title: Xanthe and the Autopsy
premise: Astrid Montrose, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has quietly exposed three 'accidental' deaths as murders, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after the funeral of her estranged mentor, Corliss Vane — a letter written in handwriting she recognizes as her own. The letter pulls her into the orbit of the Vane family's thirtieth anniversary dinner, where an alibi woven three decades ago around a drowned girl still holds the family together and its fortune intact. As Astrid uncovers that Corliss spent his final months blackmailing everyone at the table, she must choose between turning the evidence over to a police force already compromised by the family, or delivering justice herself through the one weapon no one can dispute: her memory. In the end, she forces a public confession at the anniversary toast, exposes the corrupt detective who buried the original case, and accepts that invisibility was always a lie she told herself.
about_author: Sable Quintana is a former claims adjuster from coastal Maine who spent eleven years reading death certificates before turning to fiction. She writes in a converted boathouse and refuses to own a smartphone.

chapters.title: The Letter That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Three days after Corliss Vane's funeral, a confession letter arrives — typed, but signed with a flourish Astrid remembers teaching him thirty years ago. She memorizes every detail of the envelope: the stamp, the smudge, the postmark. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in curiosity; the past knocking on a door she'd sealed.

chapters.title: Photographs of the Dead
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, flashback-laced. We learn how her memory works and how she solved three prior deaths without ever contacting police. Her handler at Meridian Insurance, Dev Okafor, warns her the Vane file is radioactive. Beat: establishing her rules — observe, never engage — and foreshadowing their collapse.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Black
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. An engraved invitation to the Vane anniversary dinner arrives, addressed in Corliss's handwriting — dated before he died. Someone wants her there. She attends the wake uninvited and catalogs eleven mourners, noting who cries and who checks their watches. Beat: the hunter realizes she may be prey.

chapters.title: The Widow's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Widow Isolde Vane's POV. Isolde rehearses the family story about the drowned girl, Lark, whose death thirty years ago built the family's insurance empire. She burns a second copy of a letter we don't yet see. Beat: cold grief laced with guilt; the reader learns the family's fortune is built on a lie.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibi
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She pulls the archived coroner's report on Lark Fenwick and finds Detective Rupe Calloway's signature on a ruling he couldn't have witnessed — he was two towns away that night, a fact her memory retrieves from a decades-old newspaper. Beat: first hard proof the original investigation was corrupted.

chapters.title: What Corliss Kept
chapters.summary: Astrid breaks into Corliss's locked study and finds a ledger of payments — six names, monthly sums, thirty years of silence. One entry stops abruptly last month. Another name is redacted with a photograph glued over it. Beat: revelation that Corliss wasn't confessing; he was collecting.

chapters.title: The Son Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Julian Vane's POV. Julian, the dutiful heir, recalls confronting his father about the ledger and being told the money protects Julian himself. He lies to his mother about where he was the night Corliss died. Beat: love curdling into complicity; Julian becomes both suspect and tragic figure.

chapters.title: A Memory of Rain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A chance encounter with the family gardener unlocks a sensory memory — rain, a blue dress, a scream by the quarry — that Astrid realizes is not hers but Corliss's, described in a letter he once sent her. Beat: the past becomes visceral; Astrid doubts her own recollections for the first time.

chapters.title: Calloway Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Detective Rupe Calloway's POV. Now retired but still paid by the Vanes, Calloway visits Astrid with a friendly warning and a veiled threat, revealing he knows about her three unofficial cases. Beat: open antagonism; the law reveals itself as the enemy of justice.

chapters.title: The Redacted Name
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Using light and pressure, she reads the photograph-glued entry in the ledger: the seventh blackmailer is Isolde herself. Cross-referencing dates, Astrid realizes Corliss was blackmailing his own wife about Lark's death. Beat: the mystery pivots — the confession letter may be Isolde's frame job.

chapters.title: Dinner Reservations
chapters.summary: Dev Okafor's POV. Dev discovers someone inside Meridian leaked Astrid's case history to the Vane family lawyer, and that his own boss signed off on it. Torn between loyalty and self-preservation, he copies the file anyway. Beat: an ally chooses courage; institutional corruption widens.

chapters.title: Lark
chapters.summary: Lark Fenwick's POV, 1994. The drowned girl lives again: her summer job at the Vane estate, her discovery of forged policies, and the night at the quarry when someone she trusted followed her to the water. Beat: heartbreak; the victim becomes a person, raising the stakes from puzzle to moral debt.

chapters.title: Two Funerals Deep
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She tracks down Lark's sister, now a hospice nurse, who gives her Lark's unsent letter naming what she found — and mentions a fourth person at the quarry whose face she never saw. Beat: grief shared doubles resolve; a new unknown enters the board.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Mapping the dinner seating against the ledger, Astrid identifies which guests' payments stopped when Corliss died — meaning whoever stopped paying is whoever killed him. Only two candidates remain: Julian and Isolde. Beat: tightening vise; deduction narrows to a terrible either/or.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde admits to the reader she wrote the confession letter — not to be caught, but to draw Astrid in, because Corliss's final blackmail demand named Astrid as his next target. Beat: reversal; the trap was baited for Astrid all along, and Isolde wants something from her.

chapters.title: Night at the Quarry
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Following the sister's clue, Astrid searches the quarry at night and finds the physical evidence Lark hid — a page of forged policy records bearing young Julian's signature as witness. Beat: the truth lands like a stone; the heir knew, even if he didn't kill.

chapters.title: What Julian Buried
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confesses to himself: at nineteen he watched his father drown Lark and took money to forget. His silence bought his inheritance and cost him everything. When Isolde asks him directly if he killed Corliss, he cannot prove he didn't. Beat: love against duty embodied; Julian decides to tell the truth at any cost.

chapters.title: Calloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: Astrid and Dev break into Calloway's storage unit and find thirty years of hush payments — including one dated the morning after Corliss died, meaning Calloway was paid after the death, not before. The killer paid him. Beat: the net closes; the corrupt cop becomes evidence.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the anniversary dinner, Astrid rises during the toast and reconstructs the entire thirty-year architecture of silence aloud, ending with the payment trail that only one person could have made the night Corliss died. Beat: climax; memory wielded as testimony, justice staged outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Glass and Water
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Cornered, Isolde confesses — she killed Corliss not to protect the secret but because his final demand was to sell Lark's story to a true-crime writer, monetizing the girl twice. She surrenders the original confession letter. Beat: catharsis and horror; motive revealed as greed wearing grief's clothing.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Calloway is arrested, but prosecutors offer Isolde a deal that would bury Lark again. Astrid releases the quarry documents and Lark's letter publicly, forcing the full record into daylight regardless of the deal. Beat: justice beyond verdicts; Astrid burns her own anonymity deliberately.

chapters.title: The Unphotographed Life
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue. At Lark's belated headstone dedication, Astrid realizes she doesn't want to remember this moment perfectly — some things should be felt once and released. She keeps a single photograph: Lark alive, laughing, in the blue dress. Beat: resolution; the woman of perfect memory chooses imperfection, and love finally outranks duty.
